aiOverview.content: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth caused by DNA alterations, resulting in tumors or blood cancers that can spread (metastasize). Diagnosed through imaging, biopsies, and blood tests, it is treated with surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy. Key prevention includes lifestyle changes. How Cancer is Diagnosed Imaging Tests: CT scans, MRIs, PET scans, and X-rays are commonly used, notes the Mayo Clinic. Biopsy: Taking a small sample of tissue for examination, which is a definitive method, says MedlinePlus. Laboratory Tests: Blood or urine tests, such as those that look for specific cancer cells or tumor markers, according to MedlinePlus. Endoscopy & Physical Exam: Procedures to look inside the body and physical exams to detect abnormalities, explains National Cancer Institute. Treatment Options for Cancer Surgery: Removing the tumor, says Wikipedia. Chemotherapy: Using drugs to kill cancer cells, according to Wikipedia. Radiation Therapy: Using high-dose radiation to kill cells, notes Wikipedia. Targeted Therapy & Immunotherapy: Treatments that target specific genetic changes or boost the immune system, explains Wikipedia. Latest Advancements in Cancer Research Immunotherapy: Continued development of CAR-T cell therapy, which engineers a patient's own T-cells to attack cancer, says a YouTube video from the National Cancer Institute. Precision Medicine: Developing treatments tailored to the specific genetic makeup of a tumor, notes the World Health Organization. Liquid Biopsies: Advancements in detecting cancer through blood tests to identify circulating tumor DNA, which allows for earlier diagnosis and monitoring. AI in Diagnosis: Using artificial intelligence to improve the accuracy and speed of imaging interpretation, notes the World Health Organization. Key Risk Factors Tobacco Use: The leading cause of cancer, accounting for a significant portion of deaths, says Cancer Progress Report. Lifestyle & Environment: Obesity, poor diet, lack of exercise, alcohol, and UV radiation, say Wikipedia and the VCU Massey Comprehensive Cancer Center. Infections: Viruses such as HPV and Hepatitis, according to the World Health Organization.
